_doc: KB-001/KB-002 issue library. Original Upfixy content. Every code a probe can emit must have an entry (enforced by tests). Severity is the default shown when a reading has no fresher context.

DNS_NXDOMAIN.title: Domain name does not exist
DNS_NXDOMAIN.meaning: When browsers ask where this address lives, the internet's address book says the name does not exist. Visitors get a 'site can't be reached' error.
causes: The domain registration expired or was suspended
A typo or missing record for this exact name (for example www)
Nameservers at the registrar were changed to a provider that has no record for it
checks: Look up the domain's renewal date with your registrar
Check whether the address without 'www' (or with it) works
Ask whether anyone changed nameservers or DNS provider recently
DNS_NXDOMAIN.next: Renew the domain if it lapsed, or add the missing record at your DNS provider. Connect your DNS provider so Upfixy can compare records directly.

DNS_SERVFAIL.title: DNS lookups are failing
DNS_SERVFAIL.meaning: Public DNS services tried to look up this name and gave up with an error. To most visitors the site looks like it doesn't exist.
causes: The domain's nameservers are not answering
DNSSEC settings at the registrar don't match the DNS provider
The DNS provider is having an outage
checks: Check that the nameservers listed at your registrar match your DNS provider
Ask whether DNSSEC was turned on or off recently
Check your DNS provider's status page
DNS_SERVFAIL.next: Contact whoever manages the domain's DNS with the message below. If DNSSEC was changed recently, that is the first thing to check.

DNS_NO_ADDRESS.title: Name has no website address
DNS_NO_ADDRESS.meaning: The domain exists, but there is no address record telling browsers which server hosts the website.
causes: The A/AAAA record for this exact name was deleted
Only mail records exist for this name
A record was moved to a different name during a migration
checks: Check whether the other form of the address (with or without www) works
Ask whether the website was recently moved to a new host
DNS_NO_ADDRESS.next: Add an address (A or AAAA) record pointing to your hosting server, or a CNAME to your hosting provider's name.

DNS_ERROR.title: DNS answered with an error
DNS_ERROR.meaning: DNS services answered, but with an error other than 'not found' or 'failed', so browsers can't get an address.
causes: The DNS provider refuses queries for this name
A misconfigured DNS zone
checks: Ask your DNS provider whether the zone is active
Check whether other names on the same domain work
DNS_ERROR.next: Send the support message below to whoever manages your DNS.

DNS_INCONCLUSIVE.title: DNS results disagree
DNS_INCONCLUSIVE.meaning: Different public DNS services gave different answers, or some didn't answer. Upfixy doesn't treat that as proof of a problem, so health shows Unknown.
causes: A DNS change is still spreading across the internet
One DNS service is having a temporary issue
Nameservers are answering inconsistently
checks: Wait for the next check
Ask whether DNS was changed in the last few hours
DNS_INCONCLUSIVE.next: If this repeats for more than a day, ask your DNS provider to check that all nameservers serve the same records.

DNS_PROBE_ERROR.title: Couldn't reach any DNS service
DNS_PROBE_ERROR.meaning: Upfixy's checker couldn't reach the DNS services it uses. This is a problem on our side, not with your website.
causes: A network issue at Upfixy's monitoring location
checks: Open your website yourself to see if it loads
DNS_PROBE_ERROR.next: Nothing for you to do. The next check usually succeeds; health stays Unknown until it does.

DNS_PRIVATE_ADDRESS.title: Name points to a private address
DNS_PRIVATE_ADDRESS.meaning: This name resolves to an internal or reserved network address. For safety Upfixy never connects to such addresses, so it can't check the website.
causes: A record points to an internal server address by mistake
The name is only meant for an office or private network
checks: Ask whoever manages DNS what address this name should point to
DNS_PRIVATE_ADDRESS.next: If the website should be public, point the record at the public server address. Upfixy will start checking it on the next cycle.

DNS_NOT_APPLICABLE.title: No DNS check for an IP address
DNS_NOT_APPLICABLE.meaning: This target is an IP address, not a domain name, so there is no DNS to check.
causes: The website was added by IP address
checks: Consider adding the domain name visitors actually use
DNS_NOT_APPLICABLE.next: Add the domain name as a website to get DNS and certificate checks.

HTTP_500.title: Website error (500)
HTTP_500.meaning: The server received the request but its website software crashed while building the page. Visitors see an error page.
causes: A recent code, plugin or theme update broke the site
A database connection problem
A configuration file error
checks: Ask whether anyone updated the site, plugins or settings today
Check if every page fails or only some
HTTP_500.next: Your developer or hosting provider needs the server's error log to find the cause. Send the message below; Upfixy can't see the log without a hosting connection.

HTTP_502.title: Bad gateway (502)
HTTP_502.meaning: A front server (such as a CDN or proxy) couldn't get a valid answer from the server that runs your website.
causes: The website application or PHP service stopped
The origin server is overloaded
A firewall blocks the CDN from reaching the server
checks: Check whether your CDN or proxy (for example Cloudflare) shows an error page
Ask your hosting provider whether the server is up
HTTP_502.next: Contact your hosting provider. If you use a CDN, mention that the CDN reports it can't reach the origin.

HTTP_503.title: Website temporarily unavailable (503)
HTTP_503.meaning: The server answered, but said it can't serve the page right now. Visitors see an error instead of your site.
causes: The hosting account hit a resource limit
The site is in maintenance mode
A recent update broke the application
The server is overloaded
checks: Open the site from another network or phone
Ask whether anyone changed the site or plugins today
HTTP_503.next: We observed the 503; we can't yet see why. Connect hosting to unlock deeper checks, or send the support message below.

HTTP_504.title: Gateway timeout (504)
HTTP_504.meaning: A front server waited too long for your website's server to answer and gave up.
causes: Pages take too long to build (slow database or code)
The origin server is overloaded or down
checks: Check if the site is slow or failing for you too
Ask whether traffic or a background task spiked
HTTP_504.next: Ask your hosting provider or developer to check server load and slow requests at the time shown.

HTTP_5XX.title: Server error
HTTP_5XX.meaning: The server answered with an error code in the 500 range, meaning something went wrong on the server.
causes: Website software error
Server misconfiguration
checks: Ask whether anything changed on the site recently
HTTP_5XX.next: Send the support message below to your hosting provider or developer.

HTTP_404.title: Page not found (404)
HTTP_404.meaning: The server is up, but says the monitored page doesn't exist.
causes: The page was moved or deleted
The website was replaced and the old address no longer exists
Hosting points to an empty folder
checks: Open the exact monitored address in a browser
Ask whether the site was rebuilt or moved recently
HTTP_404.next: If the page moved, update the monitored address or add a redirect. If the whole site is missing, contact your hosting provider.

HTTP_410.title: Page removed (410)
HTTP_410.meaning: The server says this page was removed on purpose and won't come back.
causes: The page was intentionally deleted
A site rebuild removed old addresses
checks: Confirm whether the page should still exist
HTTP_410.next: Update the monitored address to a page that should stay up, such as your home page.

HTTP_401.title: Login required (401)
HTTP_401.meaning: The page asks for a username and password before showing anything. Visitors without a login can't see it.
causes: The site is password-protected (for example a staging site)
A security setting was turned on by mistake
checks: Open the site in a private browser window
HTTP_401.next: If the site should be public, ask your developer or host to remove the password protection.

HTTP_403.title: Access forbidden (403)
HTTP_403.meaning: The server refused to show the page. Sometimes this hits all visitors; sometimes only automated checkers like ours are blocked.
causes: A firewall or security plugin blocks visitors or our checker
Wrong file permissions on the server
The site is blocked for some countries
checks: Open the site yourself on mobile data
Ask whether a security plugin or firewall rule was added recently
HTTP_403.next: If the site works for you, the firewall may be blocking our checker. Otherwise ask your hosting provider to check permissions and firewall rules.

HTTP_429.title: Checker was rate-limited (429)
HTTP_429.meaning: The server asked our checker to slow down. That says nothing about whether visitors can see the site, so health shows Unknown.
causes: A firewall or CDN limits automated requests
checks: Open the site yourself
HTTP_429.next: Optionally allow Upfixy's checker in your firewall. Health stays Unknown while it is rate-limited.

HTTP_4XX.title: Request rejected
HTTP_4XX.meaning: The server rejected the request with an error in the 400 range.
causes: The monitored address is wrong
A security rule rejects the request
checks: Open the monitored address in a browser
HTTP_4XX.next: Check the monitored address. If it is right, send the support message below to your developer.

HTTP_TIMEOUT.title: Website not responding
HTTP_TIMEOUT.meaning: Our check waited and the website never answered in time. To visitors the page keeps loading and then fails.
causes: The server is down or overloaded
A firewall silently drops traffic
DNS points to the wrong server
checks: Open the site from your phone on mobile data
Ask your hosting provider whether the server is up
HTTP_TIMEOUT.next: Contact your hosting provider with the message below. If DNS is also failing, fix DNS first.

HTTP_CONNECTION_REFUSED.title: Server refused the connection
HTTP_CONNECTION_REFUSED.meaning: The server's address was reached, but nothing accepted the connection. The web server software may be stopped.
causes: The web server service stopped
DNS points to a server that no longer hosts the site
A firewall rejects connections
checks: Ask whether the site was moved to a new host
Ask your host whether the web server is running
HTTP_CONNECTION_REFUSED.next: Send the message below to your hosting provider.

HTTP_CONNECTION_RESET.title: Connection dropped
HTTP_CONNECTION_RESET.meaning: The server started answering but cut the connection before the page arrived.
causes: The server crashed mid-request
A firewall or security system ended the connection
Network problems near the server
checks: Reload the site a few times
Ask your host whether there were network problems
HTTP_CONNECTION_RESET.next: If it repeats, send the message below to your hosting provider.

HTTP_EMPTY_RESPONSE.title: Server sent an empty reply
HTTP_EMPTY_RESPONSE.meaning: The server accepted the connection and then closed it without sending anything.
causes: The website software crashed
A misconfigured proxy or firewall
checks: Open the site in a browser and note any error
HTTP_EMPTY_RESPONSE.next: Send the message below to your hosting provider or developer.

HTTP_TLS_ERROR.title: Secure connection failed
HTTP_TLS_ERROR.meaning: Browsers couldn't set up a secure (https) connection, so they show a security error instead of the site.
causes: Certificate expired, invalid or for the wrong name
The server's https setup is broken
checks: Open the site and look for a security warning
See the SSL tab for certificate details
HTTP_TLS_ERROR.next: See the SSL check on this website for the exact certificate problem.

HTTP_REQUEST_FAILED.title: Request failed
HTTP_REQUEST_FAILED.meaning: Our check couldn't complete a request to the website for a reason other than a timeout or refusal.
causes: Network problems between our checker and the server
An unusual server response
checks: Open the site yourself
HTTP_REQUEST_FAILED.next: If the next checks fail too, send the message below to your hosting provider.

HTTP_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS.title: Redirect loop
HTTP_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS.meaning: The site sends visitors from one address to another more than ten times. Browsers give up with a 'too many redirects' error.
causes: http↔https or www↔non-www rules fighting each other
A CDN and the server both forcing https differently
checks: Open the site in a private window and see if the browser reports too many redirects
Ask whether redirect or SSL settings were changed recently
HTTP_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS.next: Ask your developer or host to review redirect rules; the redirect chain below shows the loop.

HTTP_REDIRECT_INVALID.title: Broken redirect
HTTP_REDIRECT_INVALID.meaning: The site redirects visitors, but the destination is missing or not a valid web address.
causes: A redirect rule with a typo
A redirect to a non-web address
checks: Open the site and see where it sends you
HTTP_REDIRECT_INVALID.next: Ask your developer to fix the redirect rule shown in the chain below.

HTTP_REDIRECT_BLOCKED.title: Redirect to a non-public address
HTTP_REDIRECT_BLOCKED.meaning: The site redirects to an internal address or an unusual port. Upfixy never follows those, and most visitors couldn't reach them either.
causes: A redirect rule points to an internal server
A staging or admin address leaked into a redirect
checks: Open the site and see where it sends you
HTTP_REDIRECT_BLOCKED.next: Ask your developer to change the redirect to the public address.

HTTP_REDIRECT_UNRESOLVABLE.title: Redirect to a name that doesn't resolve
HTTP_REDIRECT_UNRESOLVABLE.meaning: The site redirects visitors to an address whose domain name has no working DNS. Visitors end up on an error.
causes: A redirect to a domain that expired
A typo in a redirect rule
checks: Open the site and see where it sends you
HTTP_REDIRECT_UNRESOLVABLE.next: Fix the redirect target, or the DNS of the domain it points to.

HTTP_HTTPS_DOWNGRADE.title: Secure page redirects to insecure
HTTP_HTTPS_DOWNGRADE.meaning: The https address sends visitors to an insecure http address. Browsers may warn, and data is no longer protected.
causes: An old redirect rule from before https was set up
A CMS 'site address' setting still uses http
checks: Open the https address and look at the address bar after it loads
HTTP_HTTPS_DOWNGRADE.next: Ask your developer to update the site address and redirects to https.

HTTP_SLOW.title: Website is very slow
HTTP_SLOW.meaning: The page took more than 10 seconds to arrive. Many visitors leave long before that.
causes: Server overload or too little hosting capacity
Slow database queries or plugins
Large uncached pages
checks: Open the site at different times of day
Ask whether traffic grew or a plugin was added
HTTP_SLOW.next: Ask your developer or host to look at caching and server load at the times shown.

HTTP_NOT_CHECKED.title: Website check skipped
HTTP_NOT_CHECKED.meaning: The website itself wasn't checked this time because there was no safe address to connect to (see the DNS check).
causes: DNS is failing, disagreeing, or points to a private address
checks: Look at the Domain check for this website
HTTP_NOT_CHECKED.next: Fix the DNS issue first; the website check runs again automatically.

TLS_EXPIRED.title: SSL certificate has expired
TLS_EXPIRED.meaning: Browsers now show a full-page security warning, and most visitors will leave before reaching your site.
causes: Automatic renewal (for example AutoSSL or Let's Encrypt) failed
A manually bought certificate was not renewed
checks: Open the site and look for a 'Not secure' or 'Your connection is not private' warning
TLS_EXPIRED.next: Renew the certificate today. Your hosting provider can usually do this in minutes.

TLS_EXPIRING_CRITICAL.title: SSL certificate expires within 3 days
TLS_EXPIRING_CRITICAL.meaning: The certificate runs out in under three days. If it isn't renewed, browsers will block visitors with a security warning.
causes: Automatic renewal is failing
A manual certificate was forgotten
checks: Click the padlock in your browser to see the expiry date
Ask whether renewal is automatic on your plan
TLS_EXPIRING_CRITICAL.next: Ask your hosting provider to renew it now.

TLS_EXPIRING.title: SSL certificate expiring soon
TLS_EXPIRING.meaning: The certificate that keeps visitors' connection to your site private runs out within two weeks. After that, browsers show a full-page security warning.
causes: Automatic renewal (for example AutoSSL) is failing
The domain points somewhere renewal can't verify
A certificate was bought manually and not renewed
checks: Open the site in a browser and click the padlock to see the expiry date
Ask whether renewal is automatic on your hosting plan
TLS_EXPIRING.next: Ask your hosting provider to renew the certificate, or connect hosting so Upfixy can check AutoSSL status.

TLS_HOSTNAME_MISMATCH.title: SSL certificate is for a different name
TLS_HOSTNAME_MISMATCH.meaning: The certificate doesn't cover this exact address (for example it covers example.com but not www.example.com). Browsers show a security warning.
causes: The certificate was issued without the www (or non-www) name
DNS points this name to a server set up for a different site
checks: Compare the names listed in the certificate below with the address visitors use
TLS_HOSTNAME_MISMATCH.next: Ask your host to issue a certificate that includes this exact name.

TLS_SELF_SIGNED.title: Self-signed SSL certificate
TLS_SELF_SIGNED.meaning: The certificate wasn't issued by a trusted authority, so browsers treat the site as unsafe and show a warning.
causes: The server is still using a default or temporary certificate
Certificate installation failed
checks: Open the site and look for a security warning
TLS_SELF_SIGNED.next: Ask your host to install a free trusted certificate (for example AutoSSL or Let's Encrypt).

TLS_UNTRUSTED_CHAIN.title: SSL certificate isn't trusted
TLS_UNTRUSTED_CHAIN.meaning: Browsers can't confirm who issued the certificate, often because a middle ('intermediate') certificate is missing. Some visitors see warnings.
causes: The intermediate certificate wasn't installed
The certificate came from an untrusted issuer
checks: Open the site on a phone and on a computer; some devices may warn and others not
TLS_UNTRUSTED_CHAIN.next: Ask your host to install the full certificate chain.

TLS_NOT_YET_VALID.title: SSL certificate not valid yet
TLS_NOT_YET_VALID.meaning: The certificate's start date is in the future, so browsers reject it.
causes: A newly issued certificate with a wrong start date
The server's clock is wrong
checks: Look at the 'valid from' date below
TLS_NOT_YET_VALID.next: Ask your host to check the server clock and reinstall the certificate.

TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED.title: Secure connection could not be set up
TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED.meaning: The server accepted the connection but the secure (https) setup failed, so browsers show an error.
causes: No certificate installed for this name
Outdated security settings on the server
checks: Open the https address in a browser and note the error
TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED.next: Send the message below to your hosting provider.

TLS_TIMEOUT.title: Secure connection timed out
TLS_TIMEOUT.meaning: The server didn't complete the secure connection in time.
causes: The server is overloaded or down
A firewall drops https traffic
checks: Open the site yourself
TLS_TIMEOUT.next: If the website check also fails, contact your hosting provider.

TLS_CONNECTION_REFUSED.title: Secure port refused the connection
TLS_CONNECTION_REFUSED.meaning: Nothing accepted connections on the https port, so the secure site isn't available.
causes: https isn't set up on this server
The web server stopped
DNS points to the wrong server
checks: Try the http:// address
Ask whether the site moved hosts recently
TLS_CONNECTION_REFUSED.next: Ask your hosting provider to enable https for this name.

TLS_NOT_CHECKED.title: SSL check skipped
TLS_NOT_CHECKED.meaning: The certificate wasn't checked this time because there was no safe address to connect to (see the DNS check).
causes: DNS is failing, disagreeing, or points to a private address
checks: Look at the Domain check for this website
TLS_NOT_CHECKED.next: Fix the DNS issue first; the SSL check runs again automatically.

PROBE_UNAVAILABLE.title: Our checker had a problem
PROBE_UNAVAILABLE.meaning: Upfixy's monitoring location couldn't run checks properly at this time. This says nothing about your website, so health shows Unknown.
causes: A network problem at Upfixy's monitoring location
checks: Open your website yourself if you're worried
PROBE_UNAVAILABLE.next: Nothing for you to do. Checks resume automatically.

MONITOR_STALE.title: No recent readings
MONITOR_STALE.meaning: Upfixy hasn't received a fresh result for this site recently, so its health is unknown. This doesn't mean the site is down.
causes: A monitoring check was delayed
The site is blocking our checks
checks: Open the site yourself to see if it loads
MONITOR_STALE.next: Use Check now to queue a new check.

MONITOR_REJECTED.title: Address can't be monitored
MONITOR_REJECTED.meaning: This address resolves to an internal or reserved network, so Upfixy won't check it.
causes: The address is for a private network
A DNS record points to an internal address
checks: Confirm the public address of the website
MONITOR_REJECTED.next: Add the website's public address instead.
